stem: From which of the following sources does India obtain the maximum amount of electricity?
expl: India obtains the maximum amount of electricity from thermal sources. Fossil fuels such as coal, lignite, gas and diesel constitute the major share, with coal being dominant. Hydroelectric power and nuclear power contribute comparatively smaller shares.

stem: What is the share of hydroelectric power in the total electricity produced in India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: During the relevant period (2016–17), the contribution of hydropower to total electricity production was 10.6 percent. According to data available on the National Power Portal as of November 30, 2025, India has an installed power capacity of 509743.10 MW. Of this, hydropower contributed 50,414.66 MW, or 9.89 percent and small hydropower contributed 5158.61 MW, or 1.01 Percent.

stem: In India, the share of renewable energy in total electricity production increased from 6 percent in 2014–15 to what percentage in 2018–19?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: According to Economic Survey 2018-19, the share of renewable energy (excluding large hydropwer of more than 25 MW) in total electricity generation in India increased from 6 percent in 2014-15 to about 10 percent in 2018-19. As per data available on the National Power Portal till November 30, 2025 the share of renewable energy (including hydropower) in the total installed capacity of electricity generation in the country is 49.8 percent (hydropower accounts for about 10.0 percent).

stem: Which one of the following statements about energy production and consumption in India is not correct?

options.label: a
options.text: During the last decade, energy production in India has shown a declining trend.

options.label: b
options.text: The per capita energy consumption in the world is the lowest in India

options.label: c
options.text: The non-conventional sources of energy contribute less than one percent of the total commercial energy produced in India.

options.label: d
options.text: The industry is the major energy consuming sector in India.

expl: At the time of the question, the contribution of non-conventional energy sources to India’s total commercial energy production was more than one percent; therefore, statement (c) was incorrect. In the present context, from 2012-13 to 2023-24 (P), energy production has shown an increasing trend. Per capita energy consumption in India is not the lowest in the world. Hence, in the present context, statements (a) and (b) are also not correct. Therefore, no option is correct.

stem: In India, per capita consumption of energy in 1994 was –
expl: During the question period, option (c) was the correct answer. In India, per capita electricity consumption increased to 1395 kilowatt-hours in 2023-24, showing an increase of 45.8 percent from 957 kilowatt-hours in 2013-14. In 2023-24, per capita final energy consumption was 0.43 tonne oil equivalent.

stem:
Consider the following causes of the financial weakness of State Electricity Boards in India—
I. Sale of electricity to agricultural and domestic consumers at prices lower than the cost of production.
II. High transmission and distribution losses.
III. Lack of commercial autonomy of State Electricity Boards.
Iv. Implementation of social subsidy policies through State Electricity Boards by state governments.
Which of the above are correct?
expl: State Electricity Boards in India suffer from several weaknesses and face many difficulties, such as managerial inefficiencies, shortage of financial resources, inability to make payments to public sector undertakings, and high transmission and distribution losses. In many states, electricity is supplied to the agricultural sector at very low prices, which substantially increases the subsidy burden. Transmission and distribution losses are relatively high due to electricity theft, low-voltage supply, provision of electricity in remote and sparsely populated areas, and inadequate investment in the distribution system.

stem: Solar energy is obtained from which of the following?
expl: Solar energy is obtained from the Sun. Due to nuclear fusion occurring in the Sun’s core, a large amount of energy is continuously released. This energy radiates in all directions into space, and the Earth receives only a small fraction of it.

stem: Which of the following has the largest reserve of alternative energy?
expl: ‘Solar energy’ is the largest reserve of alternative energy; all other energy sources are limited.
